questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that it was a place in Europe, and that the university offered some exciting courses that I could use in my future career. At the same time, I love Italy, and Milan is the perfect place to go if you want both a vibrant city life and the opportunity to travel around Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy. Milan's university has a good website that's easy to navigate, where you can find useful information about the different courses and more.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. I think there was a lack of an introductory week for all Erasmus students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy, but it also required a lot of online searching and making sure we had found a trustworthy rental site that wouldn't scam us. I rented through Novecento Case with my friend, and i can highly recommend them - they are very professional and trustworthy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's a great opportunity to get a good apartment where you can potentially live with one or more people. But it's also a little expensive, but that´s just how it is in Milano.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university has a portal called Unimia, which includes a specific section for Erasmus course registration. It's very easy to register for courses or make changes if you change your mind.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an email you can contact for assistance, and there's also a how-to guide available in the portal.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, as there was no issues and I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just go into Unimia, and it's quite intuitive what you need to do

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was very similar to how a lecture would be conducted in Copenhagen. However, there isn't as much reading required to do at home.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: I guess it depend on what you study field is, but I can recommend all the four courses I took, as the teachers are very good and dedicated, and the teaching is engaging.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend dining at the many great restaurants, having aperitivo, and visiting museums, such as the Prada Fondazione, which is worth a visit. There are also many great flea markets on weekends, including one every Saturday at Navigli. I would also recommend taking a day trip or weekend trip to the cities near Milan, such as Bergamo, the Como lake or Genoa.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was fine and easy. It's not much different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The food culture, which is rich and diverse, reflecting both traditional Italian cuisine and international influence. 
I enjoyed especially the tradition for Aperitivo and their cheap coffee.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Take your time to familiarize yourself with the different courses and decide which ones you'd like to take. You might risk having overlapping courses on the same days and times, so it's good to have alternative options in mind.
2: Start your search for accommodation as early as possible. From my experience, the availability of good apartments wasn't very large, so if you want to find a nice place and avoid paying too much, it's important to start early.
3: Try enjoy your time while you're there, and experience not only what Milan has to offer but also the surrounding
cities.It
's a short semester, and time passes quickly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really besides the tree things I already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was that I had a really great teacher who taught me a lot and inspired me on what to write about in my bachelor project. In addition, I've made many new friends and truly had an unforgettable time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think I've experienced anything that was particularly challenging.
